page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes a 945 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing and small-model LLM inference text generation also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core processing, database operations, and Redis SET operations fall into the average tier. A notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth; while cached small-block reads and large-block writes perform at average levels, uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference prompt processing is also poor, reflecting limitations for massive AI workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16ads_v6 offers a balanced resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the premium cost of dedicated GPU hardware. The combination of 128.0 GB of RAM and 945 GB of local storage makes this instance highly suitable for memory-bound applications, relational databases, caching layers, and moderate data processing tasks. It is also well-suited for software compilation and web serving workloads that benefit from its strong single-core CPU capabilities.
